examples.text: Man hörte das alte Radio ein Jazzlied quäken.
Der Säugling quäkte lautstark den ganzen Tag.

glosses: A short, high-pitched sound, as of two objects rubbing together, or the sounds made by mice and other small animals.
A card game similar to group solitaire.

examples.text: "I had the very devil of a squeak for it," he went on. "I did the hurdles over two or three garden-walls, but so did the flyer who was on my tracks, and he drove me back into the straight and down to High Street like any lamplighter. […]

glosses: To emit a short, high-pitched sound.

examples.text: But I must warn you that chipboard floors are always likely to squeak. The material is still being used in new-builds, but developers now use adhesive to bed and joint it, rather than screws or nails. I suspect the adhesive will eventually embrittle and crack, resulting in the same squeaking problems as before.
If he be obstinate, put a civil question to him upon the rack, and he squeaks, I warrant him.

glosses: To speak or sound in a high-pitched manner.
To empty the pile of 13 cards a player deals to oneself in the card game of the same name.
To win or progress by a narrow margin.

examples.text: […] allowing Parkinson to squeak into the final by a half-point margin.

France were transformed from the feeble, divided unit that had squeaked past Wales in the semi-final, their half-backs finding the corners with beautifully judged kicks from hand, the forwards making yards with every drive and a reorganised Kiwi line-out beginning to malfunction.

glosses: Boğazındaki gıcıktan dolayı kesik ve ince ses çıkarmak; cızıldamak.
Gimotear o quejarse de forma aguda o infantil.
